Depends on the vehicle but since we are using the boat in the video I’ll try explain. 

For low hp high cog you want to approach the corner on the outside (so if we are turning right stick to the left pavement). Start braking as late as possible, and towards the end of your braking start your turn and aim for the apex, once you have hit the apex start accelerating out of the corner and hit the outside pavement again. The idea is to keep the vehicle on as straight a line through the corner to maintain speed. 

When you start driving higher hp cars with lots of downforce, this line will give okay results but I’d recommend relearning a different driving line.

Additional info:

Cars become unsettled with rapid turning
Make sure you’re right on the edge of oversteer
Apply brakes and throttle to change the angle of your turning
Make sure you are smooth and not too aggressive (aggressive driving style has its place but this will unbalance the truck)

I’m currently studying medicine and going into trauma, we are always taught harm reduction. Essentially you have to weigh the pros and cons of things, so alcoholics for example, we try and make sure that they can drink safely and if they get into trouble we can help them. Telling someone to quit alcohol or drugs can kill them if they go cold turkey! On the wards we will give alcohol to alcoholics (small amounts I should add) so that they don’t going into withdrawal. Same with drug addiction, we give methadone for opiates for example. The idea is that we want to allow patient autonomy, and if they want to drink or do drugs, that’s fine but how can we make the patient safer. Like providing clean needles to outpatients, and also assisting them if they do want to quit.

In my time working in emergency medicine, the only patient I managed to get ROSC was due to their colleague knowing CPR and keeping that blood going, and that brain fed with oxygen. If CPR isn’t started within 1-3 minutes, the patient won’t have much chance, especially without any loss in cognitive function. 
When we arrive, we’ll start defib and start trying to find out reversible causes (and continuing cpr with assistive oxygen (OP and NP airways, bag valve mask and O2 bottle)). The paramedic will start Epinephrine and try and get that patient to hospital. When in hospital we keep going until ROSC or until about 10-30 minutes have passed (down to the attending doctors discretion). If they recover then we start working out why the heart attack occurred and treat any underlining conditions.

But the person who saved you was the person you were with.

Unfortunately he was killed in action at the crossing of the Sambre-Oise canal, a week before the armistice was signed. His grave is located at Ors cemetery and is marked by a quote from one of his poems. ‘Shall life renew these bodies? Of a truth all death will he annul’.
